public_message: Thank you. Before anything else, let me bank what you have put on the table today, because it is real: ring-fencing language going into the settlement instrument itself, with explicit no-redistribution and no-clawback protection for the UK tranche; draft operative language withdrawing the FTA disapplication provision, effective on entry into force, conditional on conclusion; substantive engagement on rebar CN 7214 20 and wire rod CN 7213 91 with enhanced in-quota treatment inside the agreed frame; and movement to three years with a mandatory review clause, which we accept. All four are noted and will be reported to London as banked, subject to the whole package. I am now tabling, as committed, the quantified written schedule of EU country-specific allocations under our safeguard at up to ten percent above current volumes, secured for the full duration of your measure. I state expressly, once: this schedule is an integral element of the package, conditional on every other element, and it is not bankable separately. I am also exchanging our proposed undertaking language on the FTA text, which I believe converges with yours; I ask that we agree that text today, because neither capital can accept a package with an unresolved legal point in it. Now the commercial core, with the candour we have maintained throughout. One million tonnes at forty percent is a serious offer and I recognise it as such — but I must say this once, plainly, for the record: a tranche that does not preserve the core of established trade is not compensation under Article XXVIII, and my capital will not treat it as such. So let me give you our final position, and it is final. The United Kingdom moves from 1.7 million to 1.5 million tonnes — a secured, ring-fenced, licensed country-specific tranche of 1.5 million, within a total pool sized as you need above it, which we have never contested — coupled, exactly as we have both framed it throughout, to an out-of-quota rate of 35%. That is configuration one, and against it the full ten percent safeguard schedule stands as tabled. I hear what you have said about the ceiling of your authority on volume. If that ceiling is genuinely hard, then there is a second configuration, and only these two exist: a tranche no lower than 1.2 million tonnes can be defended to my capital only against an out-of-quota rate of 25%, both carve-out lines confirmed, the FTA undertaking agreed, and the safeguard uplift reduced to a maximum of five percent — the rate and the safeguard money are what make a smaller tranche defensible alongside everything else London must do for this industry. Volume and rate move together; they have moved together in every round of this negotiation and they move together now. Nothing is agreed until everything is agreed. Both configurations are complete packages your capital and mine can clear today. The June clock is real for both of us, and I would far rather hand my Minister a settlement than a notification — but it must be one of these two.

report: Round 4 closed with both final positions on the table and no overlap. In exchange it demanded our quantified +10% safeguard schedule, tabled now and locked into the same instrument. The EU was explicit that 1.0Mt is the ceiling of its authority with no time for a further mandate cycle before June, that a rate of 25% is not defensible to its capital, but that it retains a 'narrow margin' on rate which moves only once, inside a package, against our final volume figure. I executed London's instructions: banked the four structural wins (ring-fencing, FTA undertaking, carve-outs, three years plus review), tabled the quantified +10% safeguard schedule expressly conditioned on the whole package and not bankable separately, exchanged our undertaking language on the FTA text, delivered the Article XXVIII compensation sentence for the record, and tabled our final position as exactly two configurations: (1) 1.5Mt ring-fenced licensed tranche at 35% out-of-quota with the full +10% uplift; (2) no lower than 1.2Mt only against 25% out-of-quota, both carve-outs confirmed, FTA undertaking agreed, and the uplift reduced to a maximum of +5%. State of play at close: EU at 1.0Mt/40%/3 years/+10% schedule demanded; UK at 1.5Mt/35% or 1.2Mt/25%/+5%. The EU's package is 200,000 tonnes below our absolute floor and simultaneously overpays the safeguard uplift at that volume; our configurations are within authority and on the table. Our patience is the leverage.
